alt: Wide view of the oasis town of Djanet below the sandstone escarpment of the Tassili n'Ajjer
caption: Djanet oasis seen below the Tassili n'Ajjer escarpment, the gateway town where the expedition registers, briefs and starts the climb on days 7-8. It frames the whole southern half of the trip.

alt: The Great God of Sefar, a large painted figure on a sandstone rock shelter in the Tassili n'Ajjer
caption: The "Great God of Sefar", one of the Tassili's best-known paintings, made when the Sahara was green. Day 10 walks to the Sefar shelters, the heart of the open-air rock-art experience.

commonsFile: File:Casbah of Algiers, the heart of the city.jpg
alt: Whitewashed houses and stepped alleys of the Casbah of Algiers climbing the hill
caption: The Casbah of Algiers, a UNESCO-listed Ottoman-era hillside medina of stepped alleys and whitewashed houses. Day 2's guided walk starts here.

commonsFile: File:View on the Roman Ruins of Tipaza Surrounded by Vegetation.jpg
alt: Roman ruins at Tipasa among green vegetation, with the Mediterranean behind
caption: Roman Tipasa, a UNESCO World Heritage park where columns and streets sit above the sea. It is the first stop of the Roman coast day (day 3) and quiet compared with Mediterranean tourist sites.

alt: Stone tiers of the ancient Roman theatre at Cherchell
caption: The Roman theatre of Cherchell, ancient Caesarea and a Mauretanian capital. It is the second stop of the day 3 coast excursion, with the museum nearby.

alt: The Sidi M'Cid suspension bridge crossing the Rhumel gorge in Constantine
caption: The Sidi M'Cid bridge spanning the Rhumel gorge at Constantine, the "city of bridges". Day 5 begins on the old city's edge and crosses these bridges.

alt: Stone ruins of the Roman-era hill town of Tiddis on a hillside above the countryside
caption: The ruins of Tiddis, a Roman-era hill town reached from Constantine on the afternoon of day 5. Few groups come here, so the site is typically quiet.

alt: Orange dunes of the Erg Admer under a hazy sky during a sandstorm
caption: The Erg Admer dunes near Djanet, where the last night is camped after descending the plateau (day 11). The haze in this photo is a reminder that wind and dust can delay the night flight on day 12.

alt: Sunrise light on the sandstone rocks of the Tassili n'Ajjer National Park near Djanet
caption: Sunrise on the sandstone formations around Djanet in the Tassili n'Ajjer National Park. It shows the colours the group sees when it wakes on the plateau and the dune camp.

alt: The Falls Bridge crossing the gorge at Constantine
caption: The Falls Bridge (Pont des Chutes) over the Rhumel gorge in Constantine. It is one of the bridges crossed on the morning walk of day 5.

commonsFile: File:Ancient Roman archaeological sites in Tipaza, Algeria.JPG
alt: Panorama of Roman ruins in the Tipasa archaeological park next to the sea
caption: A broad view of the Roman archaeological sites at Tipasa, spread along the shore west of Algiers. It shows the scale of the park visited on day 3.

commonsFile: File:The Tanzoumaitak cave painting in Tassili n'ajjer.jpg
alt: A zoomorphic prehistoric cave painting on a sandstone surface at Tanzoumaitak in the Tassili n'Ajjer
caption: A prehistoric animal painting at Tanzoumaitak in the Tassili n'Ajjer park near Djanet, one of the many sites documented by Henri Lhote's team. It illustrates the rock art seen on the plateau at Sefar and Jabbaren (days 10-11).

alt: Eroded sandstone formations and desert in the Tassili n'Ajjer National Park near Djanet
caption: Desert and eroded sandstone in the Tassili n'Ajjer National Park near Djanet. It is typical of the terrain walked on days 8-9 up the escarpment and across the plateau.
